draft.title: C3, C4 and CAM plants
card: The problem

Rubisco normally fixes carbon dioxide. In hot, dry conditions plants close their stomata to save water, so carbon dioxide falls and oxygen builds up inside the leaf. Rubisco then reacts with oxygen, which wastes energy and lowers sugar production.
C3
plants fix carbon dioxide with Rubisco directly in the leaf cells. They have no extra way to avoid the wasteful reaction.
C4
plants separate steps in space. Carbon dioxide is first captured in one cell type, then passed to inner cells where Rubisco works at a high carbon dioxide level. Sugarcane is an example.
CAM

plants separate steps in time. Stomata open at night to take in carbon dioxide, which is stored. By day the stomata stay shut and the stored carbon dioxide feeds the Calvin cycle. Many cacti are an example.
draft.remember: C4 separates the steps in space and CAM separates them in time, both keeping Rubisco away from oxygen.

a.q: How do CAM plants reduce the wasteful reaction of Rubisco with oxygen?
opts: They take in carbon dioxide at night and use it by day
They take in carbon dioxide by day and use it at night
They pass carbon dioxide between two cell types in the leaf
They keep stomata open all day to take in more carbon dioxide
a.why: CAM plants separate the steps in time. They store carbon dioxide taken in at night, so the stomata can stay shut by day. Passing carbon dioxide between cell types is the C4 method, which separates steps in space.
a.clue: CAM separates steps by time of day.

b.q: A grass in a hot, dry region captures carbon dioxide in outer leaf cells, then passes it to inner cells where Rubisco works. What is the best description of this grass?
opts: A C4 plant, because it separates steps in space
A C3 plant, because Rubisco fixes the carbon dioxide
A CAM plant, because it saves water in dry conditions
A C4 plant, because it separates steps in time
b.why: Capture in one cell type and Rubisco use in another is separation in space, which is the C4 method. CAM plants also save water, but they separate steps by time using night and day. C3 plants have no such separation.
b.clue: Look at where the steps happen, not when.
